main_question: How do satellite AI and conventional methods compare in mapping new flood events, and how does the choice of pre-flood reference affect their performance?
central_contribution: model–information complementarity in applied flood mapping; error/coverage and preparation-resource trade-offs
reference_policies: P1 updated compatible pre-event reference under a source-fixed label-blind policy
policy_operation: replace the one pre-image; hold event image and trained weights fixed; no third-image fusion architecture
source_dataset: all5,000 held radar-change records/20events, known water-containing conditioning retained
source_fit_reuse: only exact compatible source fits; no unconditional restart of completed studies
evaluation_census: all eligible released records of the declared independent cohort and all assessable local radar cases; repeated AOIs/acquisitions remain dependent
local_case_role: Dutch/German receiving-case error and acquisition-timing interpretation; existing labels inspected before this design, not new confirmatory independent floods
gauge_data_role: event timing and measurement context, not pixel-inundation truth or a new discharge model
writing_scale: one substantial empirical article; approximately30–40main thesis-format pages plus necessary appendix, descriptive allowance not requirement

reference_policy_contract.processing: P0/P1 use the same verified processing/calibration/grid convention; any harmonized re-retrieval is explicit
reference_policy_contract.target: hold flood labels, validity and class semantics fixed across policies; retain original floodmask versus composed-label disagreements
reference_policy_contract.selection: source-fixed label-blind geometry/coverage/chronology rule; distinguish policy effect from age-only causality

evaluation_reporting_refinements: new-event primary; source-overlapping versus new-footprint diagnostic, not automatic unseen-region claim
full released-cohort coverage and temporally supported reference-agreement strata
physical-event or linked-episode dependence; event-balanced primary versus separate pixel-area totals
complete native-grid inference and overlap deduplication; no full-tile shrink to224px
external_model_role: one final source-trained state per learned pipeline per seed recommended; existing source-CV models are development evidence, not an automatic fivefold inference ensemble
preparation_status: all six source fits, external/local mapping and scoring, paired summaries and event review complete; 18,762 learned external maps preserved in 46 verified archives; local census covers 167 inputs and 14 acquisition cases
reference_interpretation_qualification: P1 precedes the provisional catalogue event date, which does not guarantee a locally unflooded reference; flood-to-permanent reclassification explains much of the observed loss, while broader water detection can be preserved
